Why does AI sometimes answer confidently, and get it wrong?
Researchers at OpenAI say a big reason is how we grade it.
On a multiple-choice exam, a guess might score. A blank always scores zero.
In one test, a model that held back on about half the questions was wrong 26 percent of the time. One that rarely held back got slightly more right, but was wrong 75 percent.
A guess has a one in 365 chance. "I don't know" scores zero.
Their fix: penalise confident errors more than uncertainty, and reward an honest "I don't know."
So, for facts that matter, ask for the source, and check it.
